papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Culture-Confirmed Neonatal Sepsis in a Tertiary Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains a major cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Early diagnosis is challenging because of nonspecific clinical manifestations and delays in laboratory confirmation. Machine learning (ML) approaches using structured electronic health record (EHR) data may improve early risk stratification in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs).
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study developed machine learning models to predict culture-confirmed neonatal sepsis using structured electronic health record data from a tertiary NICU in a low- and middle-income country setting. The goal is to improve early risk stratification where clinical signs are nonspecific and laboratory confirmation is delayed.

papers.title: Engineered Transformer Base Editor with Enhanced Editing Efficiency.
papers.abstract: Canonical cytosine base editors (CBEs) achieve precise C-to-T conversions without inducing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), yet their clinical potential remains hampered by substantial off-target (OT) mutations. The recently developed transformer base editor (tBE) significantly reduces both genomic and transcriptomic OT mutations by using a cleavable deoxycytidine deaminase inhibitor (dCDI) domain. However, the modest base editing efficiency limits its broader applications. Here, through rational deaminase engineering and fusion of a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, we developed
papers.summary: The authors engineered an improved transformer base editor (tBE) by rationally modifying the deaminase and adding a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, aiming to boost editing efficiency while retaining the low off-target profile of the original tBE. This addresses a key limitation of the tBE system, whose modest base editing efficiency had restricted its broader use.

papers.title: Decoding gene regulation in plant genomes with artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: One of the central goals of plant functional genomics is to uncover regulatory mechanisms that shape agriculturally important traits to inform crop improvement. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI), especially Large Language Models (LLMs), have greatly transformed our ability to derive regulatory information from complex genomics data. This review starts with a brief introduction of recent advances in AI and ML. We then present a plant-focused synthesis of emerging applications of AI- and LLM tools to: (i) predict epigenomic features, regulatory DNA element
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent advances in applying machine learning and large language models to decode gene regulation in plant genomes, focusing on predicting epigenomic features and regulatory DNA elements. It highlights how these AI tools can help uncover regulatory mechanisms underlying agriculturally important traits for crop improvement.

papers.title: Quantitative mapping from conventional MRI using self-supervised physics-guided deep learning: Applications to a large-scale, clinically heterogeneous dataset.
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a cornerstone of clinical neuroimaging, yet conventional MRIs provide qualitative information heavily dependent on scanner hardware and acquisition settings. While quantitative MRI (qMRI) offers intrinsic tissue parameters, the requirement for specialized acquisition protocols and reconstruction algorithms restricts its availability and impedes large-scale biomarker research. This study presents a self-supervised physics-guided deep learning framework to infer quantitative T1, T2, and proton-density (PD) maps directly from widely available clinical conventio
papers.summary: This study introduces a self-supervised, physics-guided deep learning framework that infers quantitative MRI maps (T1, T2, proton density) directly from conventional clinical MRI scans, bypassing the need for specialized acquisition protocols. The method is validated on a large-scale, clinically heterogeneous dataset, demonstrating that quantitative tissue parameters can be recovered from routine imaging. This could enable large-scale retrospective biomarker research using existing clinical MRI data.

papers.title: Deep generative models in biological sequence and structure analysis and design.
papers.abstract: Deep generative models have transformed biological sequence modeling from predictive analysis toward increasingly controllable design. Early biological applications of Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) established latent representation learning and sequence synthesis, while recent advances in transformer-based language models, discrete diffusion, flow-matching, and multimodal generative frameworks have substantially expanded the scope of biological design. This review examines generative models for DNA, RNA, and protein sequence design, emphasizing how
papers.summary: This review surveys deep generative models for biological sequence and structure design, covering VAEs, GANs, transformer language models, discrete diffusion, flow-matching, and multimodal frameworks applied to DNA, RNA, and proteins. It highlights the field's shift from predictive analysis toward controllable design of biological molecules.

papers.title: An interpretable framework applying protein words to predict protein-small molecule complementary pairing rules.
papers.abstract: Despite the high accuracy of 'black box' deep learning models, drug discovery still relies on protein-ligand interaction principles and heuristics. To improve interpretability of protein-small molecule binding predictions, we developed the PWRules framework, which applies binding affinity data to identify privileged small molecule fragments and subsequently defines complementary pairing rules between these fragments and protein words (semantic sequence units) through an interpretability module. The resulting word-fragment rules are then used by the PWScore function to prioritize active compoun
papers.summary: The authors developed PWRules, an interpretable framework that learns 'protein words' (semantic sequence units) and pairs them with privileged small-molecule fragments using binding affinity data, yielding explicit complementary pairing rules. These rules feed into a PWScore function that prioritizes active compounds, aiming to replace black-box deep learning with interpretable protein-ligand interaction principles for drug discovery.

papers.title: A Novel Unsupervised Learning Model with Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization for Predicting Substrates of Promiscuous Enzymes.
papers.abstract: Promiscuous enzymes catalyze multiple biochemical reactions, but predicting their substrate profiles remains challenging because annotations are incomplete, reliable negative labels are scarce, and enzyme-substrate relationships are inherently multilabel. Here, we present PreSEPM (Predictive Substrate Explorer for Promiscuous Enzymes), a sequence-only, closed-set framework that combines pretrained protein representations, Gaussian mixture modeling, cluster-substrate alignment, and Bayesian optimization of decision thresholds. PreSEPM operates within a predefined substrate panel and does not re
papers.summary: The authors developed PreSEPM, an unsupervised machine learning framework that predicts which substrates a promiscuous enzyme can act on using only its protein sequence. The method combines pretrained protein representations, Gaussian mixture modeling, cluster-substrate alignment, and Bayesian optimization of decision thresholds to handle multilabel enzyme-substrate relationships without needing reliable negative labels. It operates within a predefined substrate panel rather than discovering entirely new substrates.

papers.title: Multimodal alignment improves generalizability of genomic biomarker prediction in computational pathology.
papers.abstract: Computational pathology models that use digitized histopathology whole-slide images have the potential to become a cost-effective and scalable alternative to molecular assays for the prediction of genomic biomarkers, a key task in precision oncology. However, as new genomic biomarkers are discovered or quantified, large, labeled datasets must be prospectively collected to train new models. To address this challenge, we developed multimodal alignment for biomarker learning and generalization (MARBLE), a multimodal contrastive pretraining strategy that integrates structured biomarker knowledge i
papers.summary: MARBLE is a multimodal contrastive pretraining strategy that aligns histopathology whole-slide images with structured genomic biomarker knowledge, enabling prediction of genomic biomarkers from pathology images without requiring large labeled datasets for each new biomarker. This approach improves generalizability across biomarkers, offering a scalable alternative to molecular assays in precision oncology.

papers.title: Residual-Guided Hybrid Stochastic Modeling: A Two-Stage Learning Framework for Urban GNSS Positioning Enhancement.
papers.abstract: The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) has been widely adopted in navigation applications due to its high accuracy and convenience. However, in urban canyon environments, severe signal blockage caused by buildings and trees introduces substantial non-line-of-sight errors and multipath effects, leading to degraded and highly fluctuating positioning performance. To address this issue, this paper proposes a residual-guided hybrid stochastic modeling framework. The method operates in two stages: first, a pseudo-range correction estimation network takes GNSS parameters containing residuals a
papers.summary: This paper proposes a two-stage learning framework for improving GNSS positioning accuracy in urban environments where buildings and trees cause signal blockage, non-line-of-sight errors, and multipath effects. The first stage uses a neural network to estimate pseudo-range corrections from GNSS parameters including residuals, which then guide a hybrid stochastic model in the second stage. The approach aims to reduce positioning degradation and fluctuation in challenging urban canyon settings.

papers.title: Quality Variation Patterns and Predictive Modeling of Fermented Soybean Whey-Based Tofu Under Cold-Chain Conditions Using Kinetic and Machine Learning Approaches.
papers.abstract: Pre-packaged fermented soybean whey-based tofu (FSW-tofu) was stored under dynamic temperature conditions (4-20 °C) that simulated typical supermarket and e-commerce cold-chain transport modes. Changes in total viable count (TVC), psychrophilic bacterial count (PBC), hardness, springiness, chewiness, and water-holding capacity were monitored over 35 d, and a hybrid prediction model integrating mechanistic kinetics with machine learning was established. Results indicated that both temperature fluctuation amplitude and frequency significantly affected microbial proliferation and textural degrada
papers.summary: This study monitored how fermented soybean whey-based tofu degrades under simulated cold-chain temperature fluctuations (4-20 °C) over 35 days, tracking microbial counts and texture properties. The authors built a hybrid model combining mechanistic kinetics with machine learning to predict quality changes, finding that both the amplitude and frequency of temperature fluctuations significantly affect microbial growth and textural degradation.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Rheumatology and Systemic Inflammatory Diseases: From Pattern Recognition to Signal Analysis and Clinical Decision Support.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are transforming the landscape of rheumatological and systemic inflammatory disease management, offering unprecedented capacity to integrate complex, multidimensional data for diagnostic support, disease monitoring, and therapeutic decision-making. This comprehensive narrative review, based on a non-systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar combined with the authors' clinical expertise, provides a clinically oriented synthesis of current and emerging AI applications across the full spectrum of immune-mediated inflam
papers.summary: This narrative review surveys how AI and machine learning are being applied across rheumatology and systemic inflammatory diseases, from diagnostic pattern recognition to disease monitoring and clinical decision support. It synthesizes current and emerging applications to give clinicians a practical overview of the field.

papers.title: Few-shot neuromorphic vision in a nonlinear photonic network laser.
papers.abstract: With the growing prevalence of artificial intelligence (AI), demand increases for hardware that mimics the brain's ability to extract structure from limited data. In the retina, ganglion cells detect features from sparse inputs via lateral inhibition, where neurons antagonistically suppress activity of neighboring cells. Biological neurons exhibit diverse heterogeneous nonlinear responses, linked to robust learning and strong performance in low-data regimes. Here, we introduce a retinally inspired photonic computing system where spatially competing lasing modes in a random network laser act as
papers.summary: The paper introduces a photonic computing system inspired by retinal lateral inhibition, using spatially competing lasing modes in a random network laser to perform few-shot learning. This hardware mimics the brain's ability to extract structure from limited data, potentially enabling energy-efficient AI with reduced training requirements.

papers.title: The fitness landscape of a form II rubisco in a photosynthetic bacterium guides engineering of oxygen tolerance.
papers.abstract: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (rubisco) is an important but challenging protein engineering target. Fast and selective rubiscos could enhance photosynthesis in plants and accelerate biobased production processes. To facilitate engineering of rubisco, we applied an in vivo screen that couples rubisco activity to growth rate of the photoautotrophic cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803. We screened a barcoded mutagenesis library of the form II rubisco from Gallionella sp. containing 15,000 single-site and multi-site variants. Exchanges in loop 6 near the active site, at the
papers.summary: Researchers screened a barcoded library of 15,000 variants of a form II rubisco from Gallionella sp. in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis, using an in vivo growth-coupled assay to map the enzyme's fitness landscape. They identified mutations, particularly in loop 6 near the active site, that improve catalytic properties and guide engineering of rubisco variants with enhanced oxygen tolerance for improved photosynthesis and bioproduction.

papers.title: Squidly harnesses enzyme functional hierarchy and contrastive learning to efficiently predict catalytic residues from sequence.
papers.abstract: Enzymes present a sustainable alternative to traditional chemical industries, drug synthesis, and bioremediation applications. Because catalytic residues are the key amino acids that drive enzyme function, their accurate prediction facilitates enzyme function prediction. Sequence similarity-based approaches such as BLAST are fast but require previously annotated homologues. Machine-learning (ML) approaches aim to overcome this limitation; however, current gold-standard ML-based methods require high-quality 3D structures limiting their application to large datasets. To address these challenges,
papers.summary: Squidly is a new machine-learning tool that predicts enzyme catalytic residues directly from protein sequence, avoiding the need for high-quality 3D structures or annotated homologs. It combines a hierarchical representation of enzyme function with contrastive learning to improve accuracy and efficiency on large datasets.

papers.title: Biological Foundation Models for Complex Disease Research and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Complex diseases, including cancer, rare genetic disorders, neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases, arise from interactions among genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states that are difficult to capture using a single data type or biological scale. Biological foundation models address this challenge by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens and learning representations that can be transferred to downstream biomedical and clinical tasks. In this review, we examine two major model classes, genomic sequence foundation models and cell foundatio
papers.summary: This review surveys biological foundation models—genomic sequence models and cell foundation models—that learn transferable representations by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens. It argues these models can integrate genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states to address complex diseases such as cancer, rare disorders, and neurodegenerative conditions. The paper also discusses pathways toward clinical translation.

papers.title: LLM-guided prediction of riboswitch-ligand binding affinity under data-limited conditions.
papers.abstract: Riboswitches are RNA regulatory elements that sense small molecules and regulate gene expression through ligand-induced conformational changes in an aptamer domain. They enable synthetic biology applications such as biosensing and gene circuit design. Accurate prediction of riboswitch-ligand binding affinity, quantified by the dissociation constant (Kd), is essential for rational riboswitch engineering. We present a neuro-symbolic framework in which LLM-derived embeddings encode riboswitch sequences, secondary structures, and ligand representations into a unified representation that captures r
papers.summary: The authors present a neuro-symbolic framework that uses LLM-derived embeddings to predict riboswitch-ligand binding affinity (Kd) from riboswitch sequences, secondary structures, and ligand representations. The approach is designed to work under data-limited conditions, addressing a key bottleneck in rational riboswitch engineering for synthetic biology applications.

papers.title: Mapping the combinatorial coding between olfactory receptors and perception with deep learning.
papers.abstract: The sense of smell remains poorly understood compared with vision and audition. At its core is an information flow in which odorant molecules activate subsets of olfactory receptors (ORs) and combinations of receptor activations encode distinct percepts. However, predicting molecule-OR interactions, and linking them to perception, remains difficult. Here, we develop MolOR, an approach that maps odorants to their OR-activation profiles and then predicts their odor percepts. Using cross-attention between a graph neural network over molecules and protein-language-model embeddings of receptors, we
papers.summary: The authors developed MolOR, a deep learning method that predicts which olfactory receptors (ORs) an odorant molecule activates and then uses those activation profiles to predict the odor percept. It combines a graph neural network for molecules with protein language model embeddings for receptors via cross-attention, helping bridge the gap between chemical structure, receptor activation, and smell perception.

papers.title: KGTC-DDA:Drug-disease association prediction based on parallel graph isomorphism and transformer networks with cross-attention.
papers.abstract: Drug development is a complex, time-consuming, and costly process, making drug repurposing an important strategy for identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Computational drug-disease association (DDA) prediction has therefore attracted increasing attention in recent years. Although many existing methods incorporate similarity information and graph neural networks for DDA prediction, effectively capturing both local structural patterns and global dependencies, as well as modeling complex interactions between drugs and diseases, remains challenging. To address these limitat
papers.summary: The authors present KGTC-DDA, a computational framework that combines parallel graph isomorphism networks with transformer networks and cross-attention to predict drug-disease associations for drug repurposing. The method aims to capture both local structural patterns and global dependencies in drug-disease interaction graphs, addressing limitations of prior graph neural network approaches. This is a methodological contribution to computational drug repurposing.

papers.title: DLRNA-BERTa: a transformer approach for predicting molecule-RNA binding affinities.
papers.abstract: Therapies targeting RNA are rapidly expanding, with 24 FDA-approved RNA therapeutics and over 130 currently in clinical trials, highlighting RNA's growing role in drug discovery. In this context, transformer-based language models provide a scalable and cost-effective approach to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery by enabling the prediction of molecule-RNA binding affinities directly from sequence information. This study introduces DLRNA-BERTa, a RoBERTa-based framework that integrates RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to model molecule-RNA binding affinities. The framework includes six RNA class-
papers.summary: DLRNA-BERTa is a RoBERTa-based framework that combines RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to predict molecule-RNA binding affinities directly from sequence information. This transformer approach aims to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery, a rapidly growing therapeutic area with 24 FDA-approved RNA drugs and over 130 in clinical trials.

papers.title: PMPIHGLL: predicting metabolite-protein interactions using dual hypergraph convolutional networks and large language models.
papers.abstract: Metabolite-protein interactions (MPIs) play pivotal roles in regulating cellular processes and metabolic pathways and have important implications for systems biology and drug discovery. Although several computational models have been proposed, alternative approaches are needed to broaden the methodological toolkit for MPI prediction. In this study, we developed a new deep-learning model for predicting MPIs. Chemical and protein large language models were used to generate informative representations of metabolites and proteins. For each entity type, we constructed two K-nearest-neighbor hypergr
papers.summary: This paper introduces PMPIHGLL, a deep-learning model that predicts interactions between metabolites and proteins by combining chemical and protein large language models with dual hypergraph convolutional networks. The approach generates rich representations of metabolites and proteins and captures higher-order relationships via K-nearest-neighbor hypergraphs. It expands the computational toolkit for metabolite-protein interaction prediction, with potential applications in systems biology and drug discovery.

papers.title: ELISA (Embedding-Linked Interactive Single-cell Agent): an interpretable hybrid generative Artificial Intelligence agent for expression-grounded discovery in single-cell genomics.
papers.abstract: Translating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data into mechanistic biological hypotheses remains a critical bottleneck, as agentic AI systems lack direct access to transcriptomic representations while expression foundation models remain opaque to natural language. Here, we introduce ELISA (Embedding-Linked Interactive Single-cell Agent), an interpretable framework that unifies single-cell generative pretrained transformer expression embeddings with biomedical bidirectional encoder representations from transformers-based semantic retrieval and large-language model (LLM)-mediated interpret
papers.summary: ELISA is a hybrid AI agent that combines single-cell expression embeddings from a generative pretrained transformer with biomedical text retrieval and LLM-mediated interpretation, enabling natural-language interaction with scRNA-seq data. The framework aims to bridge the gap between opaque expression foundation models and interpretable, hypothesis-generating agentic AI for single-cell genomics.

papers.title: LAMBDA: a prophage detection benchmark for genomic language models.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based genomic sequence models represent an emerging frontier in computational biology. Yet, their embeddings have not yet shown the same level of predictive power as natural and protein language models, highlighting a gap between current implementations and theoretical promise. Existing benchmarks for DNA language models primarily focus on classifying regulatory elements in eukaryotic genomes, leaving open the fundamental question of whether these models learn sequence-level features across whole genomes. We introduce LAMBDA, a benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate genome langu
papers.summary: LAMBDA is a new benchmark for evaluating genomic language models on prophage detection, a task that requires learning sequence-level features across whole genomes. The authors argue that existing DNA model benchmarks focus narrowly on eukaryotic regulatory elements, leaving open whether these models capture genome-wide sequence features. LAMBDA provides a rigorous testbed for this question.

papers.title: CAREPath: semantic context-aware reasoning paths with mechanism-augmented embeddings for drug repurposing.
papers.abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs that include drugs, genes, and diseases support drug repurposing by connecting drugs to diseases through gene-mediated multi-hop paths, thereby enabling mechanism-of-action reasoning. However, deeper traversal does not necessarily improve mechanistic reasoning: long paths grow combinatorially and frequently pass through hub genes, producing irrelevant gene regulatory signals, whereas overly constrained or sparse paths may miss broader biological context. We propose Context-Aware REasoning Path (CAREPath), a knowledge graph (KG)-large language model framework inspire
papers.summary: CAREPath is a knowledge graph–LLM framework for drug repurposing that generates semantic context-aware reasoning paths connecting drugs, genes, and diseases. It addresses the problem that longer multi-hop paths often pass through hub genes and introduce irrelevant regulatory signals, while overly sparse paths miss broader biological context. The method uses mechanism-augmented embeddings to improve mechanistic reasoning for predicting drug-disease associations.

papers.title: HyLnc: a hybrid deep learning and feature-based approach for long non-coding RNA prediction.
papers.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play important roles in gene regulation, development and disease, yet accurate identification of lncRNAs from transcriptomic data remains a major computational challenge. Existing methods often rely either on handcrafted sequence features or deep learning approaches, each with their inherent limitations in capturing the full complexity of RNA sequences. In this study, we proposed HyLnc, a computational framework that integrates transformer-based contextual embeddings with biologically meaningful sequence features for improved lncRNA prediction. A custom BERT-base
papers.summary: HyLnc is a computational framework that combines transformer-based contextual embeddings with handcrafted biological sequence features to improve long non-coding RNA prediction from transcriptomic data. The hybrid approach aims to overcome the limitations of methods that rely solely on either handcrafted features or deep learning. This offers a more robust tool for identifying lncRNAs, which play key roles in gene regulation, development, and disease.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Fidelity Graph Learning for Sequence-Aware Residual Bolt Preload Prediction in Hyperelastic-Sealed Flanges.
papers.abstract: Sequential tightening redistributes load among bolts and produces a residual preload field that depends on the complete operation history. This study presents a physics-informed graph-learning framework for a 60-bolt circular flange. The model receives initial preloads and tightening order and predicts the residual preload field on a complete causal directed graph. All 1770 admissible later-to-earlier edges are retained. Among them, 240 local edges carry non-zero Elastic Interaction Coefficient Method (EICM) attributes, while 1530 distant edges remain available to learned message passing. The
papers.summary: This paper develops a physics-informed graph-learning framework that predicts residual bolt preload in a 60-bolt hyperelastic-sealed flange by modeling the full causal dependency graph of sequential tightening. The model combines known elastic interaction coefficients on local edges with learned message passing on distant edges, capturing how tightening order redistributes load across the assembly.

papers.title: PMAVP: A Mamba-Inspired Deep Learning Framework for Antiviral Peptide Identification and Functional Activity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate computational prediction of antiviral peptides (AVPs) can accelerate peptide screening and reduce experimental costs. However, existing deep learning-based methods still suffer from severe class imbalance, over-reliance on handcrafted features and limited interpretability. Here, we propose PMAVP, a multi-task learning framework that integrates the ProtT5 pre-trained protein language model with a Mamba-inspired module for AVP identification and functional activity prediction. We use ProtT5 to extract deep semantic representations from peptide sequences and a Mamba module to capture lon
papers.summary: PMAVP is a multi-task deep learning framework that combines the ProtT5 protein language model with a Mamba-inspired sequence module to identify antiviral peptides and predict their functional activity. It aims to overcome class imbalance, dependence on handcrafted features, and limited interpretability in prior methods. The approach could speed up computational screening of antiviral peptides and reduce experimental costs.

papers.title: Understanding Human Motion from Depth Sensors: Activity Recognition and Age Group Recognition Using Skeleton Data.
papers.abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) plays a significant role in various applications, from learning a discipline to physical rehabilitation. In older adults, activity patterns can indicate levels of frailty, which helps inform the design of physical training programs to prevent falls and maintain mobility. HAR sensing ranges from wearable sensors such as IMUs and RGB cameras to video, specialized gait laboratories, perturbation units, VR, and other modalities. This paper presents a comprehensive study of depth-based, skeleton-driven HAR and age group recognition (AGR) using data collected from re
papers.summary: This paper presents a study using depth-sensor skeleton data to recognize human activities and classify age groups, with a focus on applications like frailty assessment in older adults. It compares depth-based sensing to other modalities such as wearables and RGB cameras for activity recognition.

papers.title: Relative Humidity Shifts During Evaporation Enhance the Donor Differentiation Potential of Serum and Plasma Dried Droplet Patterns.
papers.abstract: The droplet evaporation method (DEM) is an analytical approach in which substances dissolved or suspended in a liquid self-assemble into characteristic patterns upon evaporation. Applied to blood and blood-derived fluids, DEM has shown potential for diagnostics. In a previous study, we identified optimal temperature and relative humidity (rH) conditions for generating two main pattern features in dried serum and plasma droplets: crystalline structures (favored at high rH) and peripheral cracks (favored at low rH). The aim of the present study was to investigate whether sequential exposure to t
papers.summary: This study examines how changing relative humidity during droplet evaporation affects the self-assembly patterns formed by dried serum and plasma droplets, building on prior work identifying optimal temperature and humidity conditions for crystalline versus cracked patterns. The findings suggest that sequential humidity shifts can enhance the differentiation potential of these dried droplet patterns, which may improve their diagnostic utility.

papers.title: Construction of a Neoantigen Prognostic Model for Gastric Adenocarcinoma Based on Multi-Omics Data Mining and the Design of mRNA Vaccines and Targeted Drugs.
papers.abstract: This study systematically explored immune targets in gastric adenocarcinoma (GAC) suitable for mRNA vaccine development. Based on multi-omics data from public databases, we first screened a set of potential tumor-associated antigen genes. Subsequently, using ten machine learning algorithms, we constructed 101 prognostic models and, through optimization and comparison, selected the Random Survival Forest (RSF) method to establish a clinical prognostic model for GAC consisting of seven genes (TYMP, IFGN, ITGAX, GBP5, GBP4, STAT1, CD84). At both the genetic and protein levels, these genes were cl
papers.summary: This study mined multi-omics data from public databases to identify tumor-associated antigens in gastric adenocarcinoma that could serve as targets for mRNA vaccine development. Using ten machine learning algorithms to build 101 prognostic models, the authors selected a Random Survival Forest model based on seven genes (TYMP, IFGN, ITGAX, GBP5, GBP4, STAT1, CD84) and further designed candidate mRNA vaccines and targeted drugs. The work provides a computational framework linking neoantigen discovery, prognostic modeling, and therapeutic design for gastric cancer.

papers.title: GDA-Pred: Generative AI-Driven Data Augmentation for Improved Prediction of IL-6 and IL-13-Inducing Peptides.
papers.abstract: Identifying interleukin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-13 (IL-13)-inducing peptides is important for drug discovery targeting cancer, immune disorders, and infectious diseases. However, experimental screening is costly and time-consuming. Machine learning and deep learning models have been developed that distinguish functional peptides from no-function ones, but their performance is limited by the small number of experimentally validated peptides. In this study, we propose a generative AI-driven data augmentation framework, GDA, and its prediction system, GDA-Pred, to improve the performance of stat
papers.summary: The authors present GDA-Pred, a framework that uses generative AI to create synthetic peptide data to augment the small set of experimentally validated IL-6 and IL-13-inducing peptides. This data augmentation improves the performance of machine learning models predicting whether peptides can induce these cytokines, which is relevant for drug discovery in cancer and immune disorders.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Deciphering the Plant Cis-Regulatory Code.
papers.abstract: Much of the regulatory information that shapes plant gene expression lies outside protein-coding regions, including many loci associated with agronomic traits. Deep learning models use DNA sequences and multi-omics data to examine components of this cis-regulatory information. This review compares convolutional, Transformer-based and graph architectures used to represent local sequence features, chromatin state and three-dimensional genome organisation. We assess their applications to transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, non-coding variant prioritisation and
papers.summary: This review surveys deep learning architectures—convolutional, Transformer-based, and graph neural networks—used to decode plant cis-regulatory information from DNA sequence and multi-omics data. It compares how these models represent local sequence motifs, chromatin state, and 3D genome organization, and assesses their applications in predicting transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, and prioritizing non-coding variants. The paper highlights both the promise and current limitations of these approaches for linking regulatory variation to agronomic traits in plants.

papers.title: Small Angle Scattering Techniques on In Situ Adsorption Studies: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.abstract: In situ and operando small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering (SAXS and SANS) have become powerful techniques for studying adsorption processes because they provide real-time information that traditional ex situ methods cannot capture. This review examines the use of these techniques in four major material groups: soft matter and polymers, carbon-based materials, biological systems and ceramics. Unlike conventional before-and-after characterization, in situ methods allow researchers to follow structural changes during adsorption as they happen, revealing adsorption kinetics, intermediate state
papers.summary: This review surveys how in situ and operando small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering (SAXS/SANS) are used to study adsorption processes across soft matter, carbon materials, biological systems, and ceramics. It highlights that these real-time methods reveal adsorption kinetics and intermediate structural states that conventional ex situ characterization cannot capture.

papers.title: Multimodal Deep Learning and Foundation Models for Early Detection and Forecasting of Plant Diseases.
papers.abstract: Plant diseases destroy 20-40% of global food production annually, posing a critical threat to food security for a projected population of 9.7 billion by 2050. Conventional diagnostic approaches relying on expert visual assessment are slow, costly, and unsuitable for modern agricultural scales. While deep convolutional neural networks demonstrated early promise, single-modality, image-centric systems consistently fail under real-world field conditions characterized by variable lighting, co-occurring infections, and cultivar diversity. This review synthesizes a decade of progress across four int
papers.summary: This review synthesizes a decade of research on multimodal deep learning and foundation models for plant disease detection and forecasting, arguing that single-modality image-based systems fail under real-world field conditions. It highlights how integrating multiple data types (e.g., imaging, spectral, genomic, environmental) and foundation models can improve early detection and forecasting for global food security.

papers.title: Cross-Virus RNA Language Models for Within-Family RNA-RNA Interaction Prediction in SARS-CoV-2 and Porcine Deltacoronavirus.
papers.abstract: RNA large language models (RNA LLMs) show potential for predicting viral RNA-RNA interactions (RRIs), but their ability to transfer between viruses remains unclear. Here, we evaluated three nucleotide language models using vRIC-seq-derived RRI datasets from two members of the Coronaviridae family, SARS-CoV-2 and porcine deltacoronavirus (PDCoV). We compared within-virus five-fold cross-validation with bidirectional cross-virus testing. DNABERT achieved within-virus AUC values of 0.9595 for PDCoV and 0.9741 for SARS-CoV-2. Under cross-virus transfer, its AUC decreased to 0.8372 when trained on
papers.summary: This study evaluates whether RNA language models trained to predict RNA-RNA interactions in one coronavirus can transfer to another. DNABERT achieved strong within-virus performance (AUC ~0.96-0.97) but dropped to ~0.84 when transferred across viruses, revealing limited cross-virus generalization. The findings highlight both the promise and the current constraints of RNA LLMs for viral interaction prediction.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analyses Identify Four Prognosis-Associated Genes in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the malignant tumors with high incidence and mortality rates worldwide. Given the poor prognosis of patients with HCC, it is crucial to explore the molecular mechanisms underlying HCC development and to evaluate prognostic markers. Differential expression analysis followed by univariate Cox, LASSO, and multivariate Cox regression identified four genes (EPO, SOCS2, IL18RAP, and KPNA2), and a Cox-based risk score was evaluated in the TCGA-LIHC cohort and externally in GSE14520 using Kaplan-Meier and time-dependent ROC analyses. Bulk, single-cell, and prot
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to identify four genes (EPO, SOCS2, IL18RAP, KPNA2) associated with prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma, building a Cox-based risk score validated in TCGA-LIHC and GSE14520 cohorts. The risk score stratifies patients by survival, offering potential prognostic markers for HCC.

papers.title: Saliency-Curated Deep Learning for Predicting Receptor Status in Breast Cancer Brain Metastases.
papers.abstract: Background: Breast cancer brain metastases (BCBMs) exhibit notable receptor discordance between primary tumors and metastases, yet obtaining intracranial biopsies is rarely practical. We created an interpretable deep learning radiogenomic model to predict estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status from MRI scans in BCBM cases. Methods: A total of 241 post-contrast T1-weighted MRIs from 142 patients were analyzed. We developed a mask-free 3D Residual Neural Network (ResNet) ensemble trained directly on cropped, bias-corrected b
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable deep learning radiogenomic model that predicts ER, PR, and HER2 receptor status in breast cancer brain metastases directly from MRI scans, avoiding the need for invasive intracranial biopsies. Using a mask-free 3D ResNet ensemble trained on 241 post-contrast T1-weighted MRIs from 142 patients, the approach leverages saliency-based curation to identify relevant imaging features. The work demonstrates the feasibility of non-invasive receptor status prediction to guide treatment decisions in this difficult-to-biopsy patient population.

papers.title: Mutation-Aware Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Binding Affinity of Nirmatrelvir Analogs Targeting Coronavirus Main Proteases.
papers.abstract: The emergence of resistance-associated mutations in coronavirus main protease (Mpro) poses a significant challenge to the development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics. In this study, we improved and accelerated a mutation-aware machine learning (ML) framework to predict the binding score of Nirmatrelvir analogue ligands against wild-type and mutant MERS-CoV Mpro. A library of 15,889 Nirmatrelvir derivatives generated through systematic scaffold modification was docked against the wild-type and five variants of the Mpro, producing a total of 95,334 structural and docking score datasets
papers.summary: This study develops a mutation-aware machine learning framework to predict binding affinities of Nirmatrelvir analogs against wild-type and mutant coronavirus main proteases. The authors docked a library of 15,889 Nirmatrelvir derivatives against MERS-CoV Mpro variants, generating over 95,000 docking datasets to train the model. The approach aims to accelerate the discovery of broad-spectrum antivirals that remain effective against resistance mutations.

papers.title: Dynamics-aware geometric learning predicts disease-associated molecular perturbations.
papers.abstract: Missense mutations and post-translational modifications (PTMs) are major molecular perturbations that reshape protein function but are traditionally studied independently. Current computational approaches largely rely on sequence conservation or static structural features, limiting our understanding of how perturbations alter intrinsic protein dynamics. We present DynGeo-Pheno, a unified geometric deep learning framework that integrates protein language model representations with anisotropic network model-derived dynamics to jointly capture evolutionary, structural, and biophysical information
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: DynGeo-Pheno is a new geometric deep learning framework that combines protein language model embeddings with anisotropic network model-derived dynamics to predict how missense mutations and post-translational modifications affect protein function. By integrating evolutionary, structural, and biophysical information, it aims to capture perturbation-induced changes in intrinsic protein dynamics that static or sequence-only methods miss.

papers.title: Potential hazard assessment of 6PPD-quinone in the context of ulcerative colitis: network toxicology, machine learning, transcriptomic analysis, and preliminary In vivo validation.
papers.abstract: The ubiquitous tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) poses potential systemic health risks, yet its toxicological impact on the intestinal tract, particularly in the context of ulcerative colitis (UC), remains largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate whether 6PPD-Q aggravates DSS-induced colitis and to identify candidate molecular events using integrative computational and experimental approaches.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone worsens ulcerative colitis, using network toxicology, machine learning, and transcriptomic analysis combined with preliminary in vivo validation in a DSS-induced colitis model. The authors identify candidate molecular events linking 6PPD-Q exposure to colitis aggravation, suggesting a potential environmental risk factor for intestinal inflammation.

papers.title: Decoding the Bone-Eye Axis: Machine Learning for Age-Related Macular Degeneration Risk Prediction.
papers.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, yet systemic determinants of its risk remain incompletely understood. Bone mineral density (BMD), a marker of skeletal and biological aging, may reflect shared pathways linking systemic and retinal degeneration. We investigated the association between BMD and AMD using a multilayered framework integrating epidemiological analyses, Mendelian randomization (MR), proteomic and metabolomic profiling, machine learning, and an experimental low-BMD model. Across 3 cohorts, including UK Biobank, National Health and
papers.summary: This study investigates whether bone mineral density (BMD) is linked to age-related macular degeneration (AMD) using a multi-layered approach combining epidemiology, Mendelian randomization, proteomics, metabolomics, machine learning, and a low-BMD animal model. The findings suggest shared biological pathways between skeletal and retinal degeneration, enabling machine learning-based AMD risk prediction from systemic markers.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning model based on multimodal MRI radiomics for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD), the most common neurodegenerative disorder, is a leading cause of cognitive impairment and dementia in older adults. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning model using multimodal MRI radiomics for the diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: This study develops an interpretable machine learning model that uses radiomic features extracted from multimodal MRI scans to diagnose Alzheimer's disease. The approach aims to provide both accurate classification and transparency into which imaging features drive the diagnosis, potentially aiding clinical trust and adoption.

papers.title: Neural Turing Machines for efficient natural language summarization: architecture, optimization, and performance analysis.
papers.abstract: Abstractive text summarization remains a fundamental challenge in Natural Language Processing (NLP), particularly for long documents that require models to preserve long-range dependencies and maintain semantic coherence. Although Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong summarization performance, their full self-attention mechanism scales quadratically with sequence length and often requires input truncation in long-context applications.
papers.summary: This paper explores Neural Turing Machines (NTMs) as an alternative to Transformer architectures for abstractive text summarization, aiming to address the quadratic scaling problem of full self-attention in long-document contexts. The authors examine NTM architecture design, optimization strategies, and performance characteristics for preserving long-range dependencies and semantic coherence without input truncation.

papers.title: ITGBL1 and RPN1 Mark a Fibrotic NP Subpopulation with Coupled Integrin Signaling and N-Glycosylation Programs in IVDD.
papers.abstract: FibroNPC is a degeneration associated subtype in intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), yet its markers and immune crosstalk remain poorly characterized. ITGBL1 and RPN1 recur as IVDD associated genes in bulk studies, but where they are expressed within the heterogeneous disc has not been resolved.
papers.summary: This study identifies ITGBL1 and RPN1 as markers of a fibrotic nucleus pulposus cell subpopulation (FibroNPC) associated with intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), linking integrin signaling and N-glycosylation programs. The findings resolve where these previously bulk-associated genes are expressed within the heterogeneous disc and suggest potential immune crosstalk in degeneration.

papers.title: Multimodal molecular features enable interpretable umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis.
papers.abstract: Umami peptides are important taste-active components in protein-rich foods, but their computational discovery is still constrained by predictors that rely mainly on sequence information and provide limited mechanistic interpretability. In this study, BioPP-GFD was developed as an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework for umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis. The model integrates molecular graphs, molecular fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors through adaptive channel attention. In the umami-bitter peptide classification task, BioPP-GFD achieved an accurac
papers.summary: This study introduces BioPP-GFD, a multimodal deep learning framework that combines molecular graphs, fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors to predict umami peptides with improved interpretability. It outperforms sequence-only predictors in distinguishing umami from bitter peptides and offers mechanistic insights into structure-activity relationships.

papers.title: Integrating machine learning and GWAS for variant prioritization in the INCIPE cohort highlights ABC transporter genes in chronic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major public health challenge, affecting approximately 674 million people worldwide and representing one of the fastest-growing causes of mortality. Since CKD is frequently asymptomatic in its early stages, the identification of novel genetic biomarkers may improve early detection and risk stratification. Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) have identified numerous genetic loci associated with CKD and related traits; however, their performance is often limited in small and imbalanced cohorts, where reduced statistical power increases both false-positive and
papers.summary: This study integrates machine learning with genome-wide association study (GWAS) data to prioritize genetic variants in the INCIPE cohort, a small and imbalanced CKD dataset. The approach highlights ABC transporter genes as potentially important in chronic kidney disease, suggesting these genes may serve as novel biomarkers for early detection and risk stratification.

papers.title: Integrating single-cell transcriptomics to construct an oncogene-driven prognostic model and elucidate metabolic-immune crosstalk in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related deaths, its progression and treatment heterogeneity are mainly influenced by driver gene and tumor micro-environment (TME) interactions. Nevertheless, the mechanisms of this process at the single-cell level remain unclear. This study integrated TCGA and multi-center single-cell transcriptome data to identify a 575 genes HCC-specific core set, developing a single-cell "oncogene scoring" system to quantify individual carcinogenic activity. This score is significantly elevated in malignant and proliferative T cells and is closely
papers.summary: This study integrates TCGA bulk data with multi-center single-cell transcriptome data to define a 575-gene HCC-specific core set and build a single-cell 'oncogene scoring' system that quantifies carcinogenic activity in individual cells. The score is elevated in malignant and proliferative T cells and is linked to metabolic-immune crosstalk, supporting an oncogene-driven prognostic model for hepatocellular carcinoma.

papers.title: BeitAI-pHLA: Multiallele Peptide-HLA Class I Binding Prediction Using Protein Language Model and Multi-Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules participate in cellular immune responses by binding to peptide fragments derived from antigens. Exploring this process is crucial to understanding the mechanisms and underlying factors that regulate the cellular immune system. Due to the extreme polymorphism of HLA, the peptides obtained from mass spectrometry of eluted ligand experiments typically correspond to multiple HLA alleles. They are thus poly-specific, providing various options for HLA assignments. This introduces notable challenges for accurate peptide-HLA assignment and interpretation. To add
papers.summary: BeitAI-pHLA is a new computational method for predicting whether peptide fragments will bind to class I HLA molecules, a key step in cellular immune recognition. It uses a protein language model combined with multi-instance learning to handle the challenge that mass-spectrometry eluted ligands often come from multiple HLA alleles at once, making binding assignment ambiguous. This approach aims to improve accurate peptide-HLA assignment and interpretation across highly polymorphic HLA types.

papers.title: Development and validation of machine learning models for 30-day mortality prediction in septic shock.
papers.abstract: Septic shock carries a high risk of death, yet traditional prognostic tools have limitations. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting 30-day mortality in septic shock patients using comprehensive admission variables.
papers.summary: This study developed and validated machine learning models to predict 30-day mortality in patients with septic shock using comprehensive admission variables. The work aims to improve on traditional prognostic tools, which have known limitations for this high-risk condition.

papers.title: DBP-CanPred: a machine learning model for predicting cancer-causing mutations in DNA-binding proteins.
papers.abstract: The fundamental cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin organization, and genome maintenance, are regulated by DNA-binding proteins (DBPs). Mutations in DBPs can alter protein-DNA interactions, leading to tumor development. However, identifying such driver mutations remains a major challenge due to limitations of experimental approaches.
papers.summary: DBP-CanPred is a machine learning model designed to predict cancer-causing mutations specifically in DNA-binding proteins, which regulate key processes like transcription and genome maintenance. The tool addresses the challenge of identifying driver mutations that disrupt protein-DNA interactions, offering a computational alternative to costly and limited experimental methods.

papers.title: Study of deep learning cues for cross linguistic part of speech tagging in English- Malayalam code-mixed data.
papers.abstract: Part Of Speech (POS) tagging is a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) that assigns grammatical labels to words in a sentence. Code mixed text, which entails switching between two or more languages within a single conversation or a sentence, presents challenges for POS tagging. This investigation entailed a comprehensive study of deep learning approaches for cross linguistic POS tagging, focused on English Malayalam code mixed data prevalent on social media platforms. The study was carried out on linguistically complex and varied English Malayalam code mixed text from social m
papers.summary: This study evaluates deep learning approaches for part-of-speech tagging in English-Malayalam code-mixed social media text, a linguistically challenging setting where speakers switch languages within sentences. The authors systematically compare neural architectures and embedding strategies to identify which cues best handle the cross-lingual, code-mixed data. The work provides practical guidance for building POS taggers in low-resource, code-mixed language pairs.

papers.title: Protein language model-generated enzyme sequences exhibit high stability in molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed protein engineering by capturing complex sequence patterns from large datasets, enabling applications such as structure prediction and functional annotation. Finenzyme applies conditional transfer learning to generate biologically plausible enzyme sequences conditioned on Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers.
papers.summary: This study evaluates enzyme sequences generated by Finenzyme, a conditional protein language model that produces sequences based on Enzyme Commission numbers, and finds that these generated sequences exhibit high stability in molecular dynamics simulations. The results suggest that language model-generated enzymes can be biologically plausible and structurally stable, supporting their potential use in protein engineering.

papers.title: Skill-File-Guided Virtual Screening: A Single-Target Formyl Peptide Receptor 2 Case Study of Large-Language-Model-Coordinated Physics and Diffusion Docking.
papers.abstract: Background: Virtual screening outcomes depend on protocol choices normally made implicitly by experts. I tested whether encoding that expertise as a "skill file" (a Markdown reference read by a large-language-model coding agent) changes virtual screening outcomes versus naive agent defaults, in a single-target case study on formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2; Protein Data Bank 7T6S, 3.0 Å cryo-electron microscopy). Methods: A Claude Code agent curated 1,000 pChEMBL ≥5 FPR2 actives and 9,829 property-matched decoys, prepared ligand libraries under naive and skill-guided protocols, and screened the
papers.summary: This case study tests whether encoding expert virtual-screening protocol knowledge into a Markdown 'skill file' that guides a large-language-model coding agent improves screening outcomes for formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2). The agent curated 1,000 known FPR2 actives and 9,829 property-matched decoys and compared naive versus skill-guided ligand preparation and docking workflows. The work suggests that LLM-coordinated, expertise-encoded protocols can meaningfully alter virtual screening performance.

papers.title: Integrating domain-specific convolutional features with Swin Transformers for transparent cervical cancer diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer screening relies heavily on manual cytopathological evaluation, which is subjective and prone to inter-observer variability. While deep learning offers automated alternatives, existing models often struggle to capture both global cellular context and fine-grained biological nuances. To address this, we propose CAMF-Swin, a novel hybrid architecture for precise cervical cell classification.
papers.summary: The authors propose CAMF-Swin, a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines domain-specific convolutional features with Swin Transformers to classify cervical cells for cancer screening. The approach aims to capture both global cellular context and fine-grained biological detail, addressing limitations of prior automated cytopathology models. The work targets more transparent and accurate cervical cancer diagnostics.

papers.title: Interpretable prediction of nucleic acid-binding proteins using a protein language model.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) and RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) is critical for elucidating transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms. However, existing computational approaches often rely on inferred labels or domain-specific annotations, which limit the subsequent generalizability.
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable computational method for identifying DNA- and RNA-binding proteins using a protein language model, aiming to overcome the limitations of existing approaches that depend on inferred labels or domain-specific annotations. The approach is designed to improve generalizability in predicting nucleic acid-binding proteins, which are key to transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulation.

papers.title: DeepVIC: modular prediction and classification of bacterial virulence factors using protein language model embeddings.
papers.abstract: Virulence factors (VFs) play critical roles in bacterial pathogenesis, and identifying these proteins and elucidating their mechanisms is essential for developing effective infection treatments. While protein language models (PLMs) have revolutionized the protein analysis, current in silico methods for classifying VFs primarily rely on fine-tuned PLMs ProtBert-BFD that perform identification and classification in a single step. This monolithic approach lacks flexibility and is vulnerable to error propagation, particularly from false negatives. Moreover, the direct use of PLM embeddings as feat
papers.summary: DeepVIC introduces a modular framework for predicting and classifying bacterial virulence factors by separating the identification step from the classification step, using protein language model embeddings as features. This design improves flexibility and reduces error propagation compared to monolithic fine-tuned models like ProtBert-BFD. The approach offers a more robust in silico tool for studying bacterial pathogenesis.

papers.title: Computational mapping of resistance-relevant signals in proteins using deep and classical feature spaces.
papers.abstract: The functional diversity of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) proteins necessitates advanced computational frameworks capable of capturing complex macromolecular signatures beyond simple sequence homology. While traditional alignment-based tools identify known resistance determinants, they often overlook the underlying biochemical and structural properties that define novel or divergent resistant macromolecules.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that maps antimicrobial resistance (AMR) proteins using both deep learning and classical feature representations, aiming to capture biochemical and structural signatures beyond simple sequence homology. The approach is designed to detect novel or divergent resistance determinants that alignment-based tools typically miss. It highlights the value of combining feature spaces for functional annotation of AMR proteins.
